results.evidence: The tests pin utc_now to 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z (tests/test_approve.py:15,21) and store lead 1. test_lead_approval_is_recorded_with_its_reference (line 69) runs 'approve lead 1 --approver Founder --reference "email 2026-11-29 Re: first prospects"'. It asserts exit 0 and stdout 'approval 1 recorded: lead 1 by Founder'. It asserts one approval activity with lead_id 1 and payload {scope: lead, item: '1', approver: Founder, reference: the given text, approved_on: '2026-11-30'}. test_date_sets_the_approval_day (line 89) with --date 2026-11-29 records approved_on '2026-11-29'. The implementation matches: cottonwood/gate.py builds the payload, and cottonwood/cli.py:_run_approve defaults the day to Denver today and passes --date through. All 20 tests in tests/test_approve.py passed.

The draft branch of gate._apply requires --lead, checks that the lead exists, stores the item, and adds payload['sha256'] as the hex SHA-256 of the file's bytes. The activity is inserted with lead_id. Approval.line() prints 'approval N recorded: draft ITEM for lead L by APPROVER', where N is the activity id. tests/test_approve.py::test_draft_approval_stores_its_lead_and_digest checks the exact stdout, lead_id 1, scope 'draft', item equal to the draft argument, and sha256 equal to hashlib.sha256(draft.read_bytes()).hexdigest(). All 20 tests in tests/test_approve.py passed. One minor point: the item is stored after .strip(), so it differs from the argument only if the argument has surrounding whitespace.

In cottonwood/gate.py, the audience and offer scopes share one branch. It stores the stripped item as the text. It checks the lead only when lead_id is not None, and it passes lead_id (None by default) to the activity insert. So lead_id is NULL without --lead and the given lead id with --lead 1. The approve CLI command takes --approver, --reference and --lead. tests/test_approve.py covers audience and offer without --lead: exit 0, the printed line, lead_id None, and scope and item in the payload (lines 122-135). It covers offer with --lead 1: exit 0 and lead_id 1 (lines 138-142). Audience with --lead 1 has no test of its own, but it runs through the same code branch as offer. The tests in tests/test_approve.py all passed (20 passed).

tests/test_approve.py parametrizes all 12 refusal cases the AC lists. The cases are blank and missing reference, blank approver, lead 99, lead abc, draft without --lead, a missing draft file, blank audience and offer items, --date 2026-12-01, --date 30/11/2026, and offer x --lead 99. Each case asserts exit 1 (EXIT_REFUSED), exactly one stderr line starting with the expected prefix, and no rows in activities. test_an_unknown_scope_is_a_usage_error asserts that 'approve vendor x' exits EXIT_USAGE with nothing appended. I ran these with pytest and all 13 selected tests passed (20/20 in the file). The implementation is consistent with this. gate.py raises GateError with 'field: message', and cli.py:_run_approve prints 'error: {exc}' and returns EXIT_REFUSED. A bad date goes through events.EventError, which gives the 'error: date:' prefix. The scope argument uses argparse choices, so an unknown scope is rejected with a usage error. I did not separately confirm that EXIT_USAGE equals 2. The test passing against argparse's own usage-error exit code is consistent with 2.

Ran in the worktree with UV_OFFLINE=1 UV_NO_SYNC=1. uv run pytest: 738 passed, exit 0. uv run ruff check .: All checks passed!. uv run mypy .: Success, no issues found in 77 source files. uv run ruff format --check .: 241 files already formatted. The 'ruff 0' line in the output is the exit code of the piped tail, not of ruff, but the message itself shows the check passed.

git diff a774d6b for tests/test_no_send_credentials.py is purely additive. It adds a PLANNING_RECORDS = 'work/' constant, an _is_exempt() helper, a parametrized test_only_planning_records_are_exempt, and one `if _is_exempt(...): continue` line in the repo scan. No base lines were removed or changed. The matcher regexes, CREDENTIAL_NAMES, the flagged and harmless parametrized cases, the .env.example test and the this_file skip are all untouched. The only behavior change is that tracked paths starting with 'work/' are skipped. That matches the stated reason. On the base, git-tracked work/ files (work/done/CCGE-113.md, work/specs/research-skill/spec.md and others) quote the sample credential strings as criterion text. The exemption is narrow: the test shows 'tests/work/fixture.env', '.env.example' and 'config/pilot.yaml' are not exempt. The file's tests pass (25 passed).
